# APEX browser lifecycle patches

This source subset is copied from `github.com/mxschmitt/playwright-go v0.6100.0`. Its MIT license remains in LICENSE. UPSTREAM_MANIFEST.json records the pristine copied-file hashes and the verified module zip checksum. README.upstream.txt preserves the upstream README byte-for-byte with its original path declared in UPSTREAM_MANIFEST.json; its relative links belong to omitted upstream assets. README.md is a local wrapper linking this contract, the license and pinned upstream documentation. Upstream native integration assets, commands, scripts, examples and CI are not included.

browser_context.go changes from copied upstream source: Close uses atomic entry CAS, its complete body moves below the ordinary early-nil guard, and its once close notification broadcasts by closing the existing buffered channel. The entry winner assigns closeReason under the same lock used by its reader. owned_har_close.go adds the optional OwnedHARBrowserContext.CloseHAROwned method, which reserves a fresh entry, joins ordinary repeat owned callers, retains complete result/error, and fails closed for prior ordinary/server entry or abnormal completion. owned_har_close_test.go tests this extension. An unfinished repeat from the exact synchronous SDK dispatcher or an unknown dispatcher identity fails closed without poisoning the first owner or blocking its acknowledgment; completed receipts remain available on every goroutine. Generated interfaces and Playwright/Node/browser/platform pins are unchanged.

APEX capture ownership uses the optional method; unsupported SDKs cannot claim writer completion. The local module replacement affects every project build using the SDK. Run extension contract tests explicitly with `go test -race github.com/mxschmitt/playwright-go -run '^TestAPEXOwnedHAR' -count=1`; root `go test ./...` does not run dependency-module tests. Copied upstream native-install/process-kill tests are outside this focused command. Existing controlled browser/recording fixtures remain the native compatibility gates. Unknown prior/server-close ownership stays protected; this patch is not a general crash cleanup guarantee.

`frame.go` additionally serializes load-state snapshots and waiter registration with native load-state updates. Previously a completed load could arrive after a negative snapshot but before listener registration, leaving a successful navigation waiting for an event already delivered. The narrow lock is released before waiting, invoking callbacks or emitting native events. No synthetic load event, longer timeout, browser/driver version change or target probe is introduced. `load_state_registration_test.go` deterministically injects that transition and checks ready, timeout, closed-page and listener-cleanup behavior. Run it explicitly with `go test -race github.com/mxschmitt/playwright-go -run '^TestAPEXLoadState' -count=1`, together with the owned-HAR extension tests and actual Chromium/WebKit navigation fixtures. The upstream source hashes remain pristine provenance; the manifest explicitly lists the altered files.


`request.go` now returns a detached timing snapshot under a narrow mutex. The same mutex serializes native completion updates and response timing initialization (`response.go`). A caller inspecting navigation timing can no longer race a late response completion or mutate the SDK's internal record through its returned pointer. Missing timing remains missing; partial native initializers preserve previously observed fields. No clock value, navigation event or target request is synthesized. `request_timing_snapshot_test.go` checks detached snapshots, partial initializers and concurrent readers/writers. Run it with `go test -race github.com/mxschmitt/playwright-go -run '^TestAPEXRequestTiming' -count=10`; dependency tests must run explicitly because the root suite does not include this module.

`frame.go` also snapshots the exact successful new-document request and an incrementing native navigation sequence under its existing mutex. Same-document, failed and missing-request events advance the sequence and clear the request. `apex_navigation_commit.go` adds `APEXFrameNavigationCommit`, which exposes a detached pair; it does not infer identity from URLs or initializers, and does not itself prove a DOM lifecycle. Consumers must bracket their document-identity observation with unchanged native sequence/request snapshots. `apex_navigation_commit_test.go` covers invalidation and concurrent atomic snapshots. Run `go test -race github.com/mxschmitt/playwright-go -run '^TestAPEXNavigationCommit' -count=10`; the root suite does not include dependency-module tests. Browser/driver/platform pins are unchanged.
